text.p: Germany may have unearthed a new tennis star in 19-year-old Tommy Haas, who overcame his second seeded opponent in four days on Friday to reach the semifinals of the German Open.

Haas, who left school less than a year ago and entered the tournament as a wildcard, beat the 11th-seeded Spanish clay court expert Alberto Berasategui 2-6 6-3 6-3 to the delight of 12,000 local supporters in the Rothenbaum stadium.
On Wednesday, the 123rd-ranked Haas beat third-seeded Spaniard Carlos Moya, the Australian Open finalist, in straight sets and even Boris Becker has been impressed.

"He has the potential to get into the top 50 or even higher - very soon," said Becker, who has helped train Haas. On today's evidence he may soar a great deal higher - and even sooner than many expect.
Haas, based at Nick Bollettieri's tennis academy in Florida, played a remarkably mature game to overcome both his nerves and a fast-moving baseline opponent with a great deal of experience on clay.
"I was very, very nervous, as this was a new experience and I had no chance in the first set," said Haas.
"But it was great to have such support and when I felt more confident I just tried to give it all I had."

His all included a good all-court game and an alert awareness of when Berasategui, who was made to do a great deal of running, might be flagging sufficiently to become vulnerable to drop-shots or attacks from the net.

In the fifth game of the final set Haas produced, in successive rallies, a drop-shot winner from five feet behind the baseline, a backhand half-volley drop winner while attemptimg to serve and volley, and a forehand drop-shot which was angled so wide it opened up the court for an easy backhand pass.
Soon he was serving an ace to reach match point, and then fastened on to a net-cord which fell short to make a winning approach to the net.
Haas' reward is a semifinal against another Spaniard, Felix Mantilla, the conqueror of Becker yesterday (Thursday) and now the conqueror of giantkiller Hicham Arazi.

Mantilla beat Arazi 4-6 7-6(8-6)6-4, but the France-based Moroccan, who had beaten the top-seeded Thomas Muster, was not far from bringing down his second-seeded opponent, again showing great imagination and flair.

Arazi led 5-4 in the second set, and 5-4 in the tie-break. Twice he was within two points of victory, but on both occasions the 10th seed showed a sounder appreciation of how to win the most crucial points.
